subject: TTFT probe scheduling and chunk-emit commitment
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena@opsly.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ava_chen@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: TTFT probe scheduling and chunk-emit commitment

Hi Lena — thanks again for the productive demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope a short performance probe focused on TTFT and streaming behavior.

Recap from the call (our understanding):
- Primary goal: hit consistent Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) targets for short/interactive prompts used in Opsly's live assistant.
- Preferred streaming: you mentioned you’d prefer a persistent connection (WebSocket) but are open to SSE for fallbacks.
- Rough targets you cited: median TTFT ~50ms for short prompts, p95 target under ~120ms during steady traffic.
- Typical workloads: 256-token context, ~120-token outputs on average; spikes up to ~400 tokens for long-answer flows.
- Concurrency/throughput: steady concurrency ~300–500, peak bursts to ~1,200; would like graceful degradation and chunk cadence that makes partial answers useful.

Proposed probe scope:
- Controlled test window: 2–3 days, run synthetic traffic (we’ll provide harness) with both steady-state and burst phases.
- Metrics we’ll measure: TTFT (p50/p95/p99), chunk latency (inter-chunk gap), tokens/sec, client-visible first-chunk size, error rate under load.
- Streaming modes: primary test over WebSocket; fallback SSE run separately to compare chunk cadence/latency.

Immediate asks from Opsly (what we need from you):
- Confirm preferred test dates (we propose 2027-05-25 to 2027-05-27).
- Confirm expected payloads: typical context and output token lengths for the two main flows (short-interactive vs long answer).
- Any IP/port whitelisting required on your side or will you run the harness from your environment?

Attachments: I’ve attached a draft probe plan (ttft_probe_plan_v1.pdf) and a short SLA/questions doc listing telemetry we’ll collect (opsly_sla_questions.pdf).

Next steps / owners:
- Marcus (me): finalize probe plan, provide harness and test instructions once we confirm date.
- Karthik: will own runtime configuration suggestions (batching/quantization tradeoffs) and watch the pilot.
- Ava: will coordinate any security/whitelisting and collect your network constraints.
- Lena / Opsly: confirm dates and provide the two representative payload samples.

If that matches your expectations I’ll lock the test window and share the harness link + HubSpot record.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Lena Park <lena@opsly.ai>

Cc: eng@opsly.ai, devops@opsly.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:47:15 -0700
Subject: Re: TTFT probe scheduling and chunk-emit commitment

Marcus — thanks for the solid summary. A few clarifications from our side and confirmations:

1) Streaming preference: we do prefer WebSocket persistent connections for the assistant; we fall back to SSE for environments where websockets are restricted. Please ensure the probe exercises both modes if possible.

2) TTFT targets: to be concrete — our business goal is p95 <= 100ms for short prompts (user < 40 tokens) and median ~50ms. For longer answers we can tolerate higher p95 but would expect first token within ~200ms in most cases.

3) Concurrency profile: our steady concurrency is ~400 concurrent open sessions; typical short-term bursts during peak are ~1.2k concurrent connections. Traffic is spiky (user-driven).

4) Payload profiles: short-interactive flow: ~20–40 token prompt, 40–120 token reply. Long-answer flow: 300–400 token context, 300+ token output (less frequent).

5) Pilot ask: we’d like Redwood to run an initial 50-concurrency WebSocket probe from your hosted infra to validate TTFT and chunk cadence, then we’ll run a second pass from our region to verify network effects. If you can provide a test harness and an initial results summary within 48 hours of the probe, that would be ideal.

6) Security: we will likely need an IP range to whitelist for inbound callbacks; we’ll confirm with our network team but please share any IPs you plan to use.

We are available 2027-05-25 morning PST or 2027-05-26 afternoon PST for the test window. Please confirm and we’ll calendar it.

Thanks — Lena
Lena Park
Head of Platform, Opsly\lena@opsly.ai | +1 206-555-0199

- Proposed probe window: 2027-05-25 08:00–12:00 PST (Redwood-hosted WS probe, 50 concurrency steady + 3 burst phases) and 2027-05-26 14:00–17:00 PST (Opsly-run probe from your environment).
- Deliverables from Redwood: harness repo + runbook URL, expected result dashboard (Grafana snapshot), and a short executive summary by EOD after each probe run.
- Metrics thresholds we’ll report against: TTFT p50/p95/p99, first-chunk byte size, inter-chunk median gap, error rate, and estimated cost/tokens for the run.
- Whitelisting: we’ll use the following IPs for the Redwood-hosted probe: 35.82.142.10/32, 35.82.142.11/32. Please confirm if those are acceptable or if you need a CIDR block instead.

Action items:
- Marcus: share harness + updated probe plan (attached) — ETA EOD 2027-05-19.
- Ava: please share any security docs required for whitelisting.
- Karthik: will draft runtime config suggestions tuned for low-TTFT (smaller batch sizes, aggressive KV cache priming, lightweight quantized variant).

I’ve attached an updated probe plan (ttft_probe_plan_v1.pdf) that includes the exact traffic phases. If the dates and IPs look good I’ll calendar the Redwood-hosted run.

Thanks — Marcus
